stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Water in a beaker on a hot plate. The plate delivers power $P$ to a mass $m$ of water. Slide $P$ and $m$, watch $T(t)$ climb. Get the water to $80\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ at least once with each slider moved.
stages.concept: Sensible heat: $Q = m\,c\,\Delta T$ where $c \approx 4180\,\mathrm{J\,kg^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$ for water. With constant power, $T(t) = T_0 + k\,t$ where the slope $k = \dfrac{P}{m\,c}$ has units of $^\circ\mathrm{C}/s$.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Hit the orange crosshair: reach temperature $T^{*}$ at exactly time $t^{*}$. Tune $P$ and $m$ so your line passes through the target.
stages.concept: Any pair $(P, m)$ works as long as the slope matches: $k^{*} = \dfrac{T^{*} - T_0}{t^{*}} = \dfrac{P}{m\,c}$. Doubling $P$ and $m$ together keeps $k$ unchanged.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: Only the target line is drawn. Read its slope $k^{*}$ from the graph on paper, pick $P$ and $m$ blind, then press RUN. Match $k$ to within $\pm 3\%$.
stages.concept: Read two points from the target line to get $k^{*} = \dfrac{\Delta T}{\Delta t}$. Then any $(P, m)$ with $\dfrac{P}{m\,c} = k^{*}$ works. Peek gives you a reading method — not the answer.

labels.tip1: move P and m sliders, then let the water climb to 80°C at least once
labels.tip2: tune P and m so your line passes through the orange crosshair
labels.tip3: read k* = ΔT/Δt from the target line, then set P/(m·c) = k*
labels.peek_hint: read the slope: pick two points on the target line, k = (T2 − T1) / (t2 − t1) in °C/s; then set P/(m·c) = k

1.1: Larger P heats faster. Larger m heats slower. The slope k = P/(m·c) is what matters.
1.2: The dashed 100°C line marks boiling. With c ≈ 4180 J/kg·K, k has units of °C/s.
1.3: Doubling P and doubling m at the same time keeps the slope k unchanged.

2.1: Compute the target slope: k* = (T* − T0) / t*. Then set P and m so P/(m·c) = k*.
2.2: Pick m first (say m = 0.5 kg), then P = k* · m · c gives you the power to dial in.
2.3: Fine-tune with the m slider once you're close; small m changes = small k changes.

3.1: Pick two points on the target line. Slope k* = (T2 − T1) / (t2 − t1) in °C/s.
3.2: For water c ≈ 4180 J/kg·K. So P/m = k* · c gives you the required ratio.
3.3: Press Peek for the reading method. Then set P and m so P/(m·c) = k*, and press RUN.
